title: OME · Multi-cluster control plane
description: Fan-out health for the OME multi-cluster control plane: fleet membership, per-ISVC placement and declared policy, tenant quota on the members, and control-plane component health. Every query pins endpoint="metrics" because the OME pods are scraped twice and unfiltered aggregates double-count; gauges collapse per-pod series with max by (...) so a controller rollout neither splits a line nor inflates a count.

panels.title: Workload clusters
panels.description: Members whose Ready condition is True, over all members registered on this control plane. Below total means a member is unreachable. max by (cluster) collapses the per-pod series so a controller rollout does not inflate the count.

panels.title: Allocatable accelerators
panels.description: Schedulable accelerators over all accelerators present on the selected members. The gap is the unavailable pool: cordoned, unhealthy or parked. Cluster-wide -- capacity metrics carry no quota label, so $tenant does not narrow this.

panels.title: Governed quota
panels.description: Total nominal quota handed to tenants across the selected members. Spans ALL tenants regardless of $tenant, so it is the fleet-wide governed total.

panels.title: Quota usage
panels.description: Admitted over governed across all tenants. Approaching 100% means quota, not hardware, is the ceiling. clamp_min avoids divide-by-zero when nothing is governed.

panels.title: Total tenants
panels.description: Distinct quota tenants on the selected members. Spans ALL tenants regardless of $tenant.

panels.title: Total ISVCs
panels.description: InferenceServices the placement controller manages on this control plane, in every phase.

panels.title: Failed placements
panels.description: ISVCs whose placement failed terminally. Zero is healthy; the natural alert target.

panels.title: OME control plane errors
panels.description: Reconcile errors across both OME control-plane components, counted over the selected time range so the number follows the time picker. Shown whole because increase() extrapolates. Container restarts live per component further down.

panels.title: Managed object counts (control plane etcd)
panels.description: Straight from the control plane apiserver, so it still counts objects when a controller is wedged.

panels.title: Member readiness over time
panels.description: 1 = Ready, 0 = not. Collapsed with max by (cluster) so a controller rollout does not split each member into one broken segment per pod generation.

panels.title: Member state
panels.description: Current Ready condition per member with its reason, one row per member.

panels.title: WorkloadCluster reconcile rate and errors
panels.description: Connection probes run on a health interval, so a flat non-zero rate is normal. A rising error rate means members are unreachable.

panels.title: ISVCs by placement phase
panels.description: Pending = nothing matched or nothing connected. Admitting = fanned out, not yet admitted. Placed = admitted. Failed = terminal. Racing is the legacy name for Admitting and may appear during upgrades.

panels.title: Placement phase
panels.description: The namespace arrives as exported_namespace because the controller pod's own namespace already owns the namespace label on this scrape path.

panels.title: Where each ISVC landed
panels.description: Every cluster this ISVC was fanned out to. Admitting means the derived ISVC exists but has not been admitted; legacy Placed may appear with the same meaning during upgrades. Single mode expects one Admitted winner; All and Split list every serving home.

panels.title: Declared placement policy
panels.description: What the ISVC asked for, from spec.placement. Diff this against 'Where each ISVC landed' to see intent against outcome.

panels.title: Replicas per home (admitted vs ready)
panels.description: Admitted is what the home's Kueue let through; ready is what actually serves. A persistent gap means pods are admitted but not starting.

panels.title: Nodes (cluster)
panels.description: Nodes backing member capacity, all states.

panels.title: Unattributed (cluster)
panels.description: Accelerators no quota claims. Zero on a member that ran a capacity pass and found nothing wrong; No data on one that measured no capacity at all. The family is absent in both cases, so the fallback is scoped to allocatable rather than unconditional -- a fake zero and a blank panel are each wrong for one of them.

panels.title: Capacity: allocatable vs unavailable
panels.description: Capacity on the selected members by resource and flavor. Cluster-wide.

panels.title: Nodes by state
panels.description: Node population by state. Cluster-wide.

panels.title: Kueue objects written
panels.description: The materializer's write path into Kueue. Flat zero while workloads wait means projection is stalled. Carries no quota label, so it is cluster-wide.

panels.title: Unattributed accelerators by reason
panels.description: Which fix an unclaimed accelerator needs. NoMatchingFlavor means no ResourceFlavor's node labels matched; AmbiguousFlavor means two matched equally well, so attributing the node to either would be a guess. The total above says something is wrong -- this says what, and they need different repairs.

panels.title: Unattributed nodes by reason
panels.description: Distinct machines, not node-resource pairs: a node advertising two unclaimed resources counts once. Read against the panel to its left to tell one badly labelled machine from a whole pool.

panels.title: Kueue objects reaped
panels.description: The other half of the write path. materialize is routine orphan collection when the tree no longer names an object; finalize is a node being deleted. Written without reaped cannot show a churn loop, where the materializer rewrites every pass what the sweep has just removed.

panels.title: Admitted (tenant)
panels.description: Admitted against tenant quota. Follows $tenant.

panels.title: Reserved not admitted
panels.description: Quota held but not serving. Sustained non-zero means workloads are stuck in admission. Follows $tenant.

panels.title: Borrowed (tenant)
panels.description: Borrowed from other tenants' unused quota. Follows $tenant.

panels.title: Nominal vs admitted by tenant
panels.description: Granted quota against what is admitted, per tenant.

panels.title: Utilization by tenant
panels.description: Admitted over nominal per tenant. Sustained near 1 means the tenant is quota-bound.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager ready
panels.description: Available over desired replicas.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager leader
panels.description: Must be exactly 1. Zero means no active leader and nothing reconciles; above 1 means split brain.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager restarts
panels.description: Container restarts over the selected time range.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager CPU (cores)
panels.description: Per-pod CPU. Only the leader does real work, so one hot pod is expected.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident set size per pod.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager reconcile rate by controller
panels.description: Work actually being done, per controller.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager reconcile errors
panels.description: Sustained non-zero means a controller cannot make progress.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager reconcile p99
panels.description: Tail reconcile latency. Cross-cluster fan-out makes the placer slower than a local controller.

panels.title: ome-controller-manager queue depth / saturation
panels.description: Oldest unfinished item in seconds, plus active over max workers. Saturation pinned at 1 means the controller is the bottleneck.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager ready
panels.description: Available over desired replicas.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager leader
panels.description: Must be exactly 1. Zero means no active leader and nothing reconciles; above 1 means split brain.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager restarts
panels.description: Container restarts over the selected time range.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager CPU (cores)
panels.description: Per-pod CPU. Only the leader does real work, so one hot pod is expected.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident set size per pod.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager reconcile rate by controller
panels.description: Work actually being done, per controller.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager reconcile errors
panels.description: Sustained non-zero means a controller cannot make progress.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager reconcile p99
panels.description: Tail reconcile latency. Cross-cluster fan-out makes the placer slower than a local controller.

panels.title: ome-quota-manager queue depth / saturation
panels.description: Oldest unfinished item in seconds, plus active over max workers. Saturation pinned at 1 means the controller is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Apiserver client calls by code
panels.description: Control-plane apiserver traffic from the OME components. A rise in 4xx or 5xx precedes reconcile errors.

panels.title: Webhook requests by code
panels.description: Admission webhook traffic. The placer disables the ISVC webhooks in control-plane role, so quiet is expected here.

panels.title: What this board cannot tell you, and the fix for each

options.content:
The placement stack registers its own metrics, so member health, per-ISVC placement and declared policy are first-class here rather than inferred from generic signals. Quota lives here too, rather than on a board of its own: capacity is the denominator every tenant number is read against, and the two were being kept in step by hand.

Cohort rows are absent from the tenant panels on purpose -- a cohort's nominal contains its children's, so a sum over both double-counts every leaf. What remains uncovered:

| Gap | Why it is missing | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| InferenceService *serving* state — Ready, failed, in-progress per namespace | The platform kube-state-metrics on a management cluster carries no OME `customResourceState` config, so every `ome_inferenceservice_*` series is absent. Placement phase is exported, but that is where the ISVC was put, not whether it serves. | Add `config/monitoring/kube-state-metrics-config.yaml` to that KSM. Config only, no OME code change. |
| Whether quota accounting matches reality | Where Kueue does not gate serving pods, admitted counts read zero while accelerators are consumed, so a healthy zero and an unmeasured fleet look identical. | A pod-derived consumption metric split by whether Kueue governs the pod. |
| Where a tenant's share landed across members | `status.budgets[].perCluster` carries it; no metric exports it. The tenant row sums the members selected, so an uneven split reads the same as an even one. | Export the per-cluster breakdown the projection already computes. |
| Tree structure — parent, depth, violations by reason | The path label ships in the budget family but nothing reads it yet, so a tenant is a flat name rather than a position. | Label the tenant panels by path, and export the violation reasons the tree check already produces. |
| Fan-out latency and sweep lag | Computed by `tests/perf/multicluster` offline and nowhere in production. The phase gauge shows the outcome, not how long the race took or how long a loser's derived object survived. | Placement histograms around fan-out and the loser sweep. |
Nothing on this board pages anyone: `prometheusRule.enabled` is false everywhere, no PrometheusRule object is deployed, and Alertmanager has no route or receiver. `Failed placements` and `OME control plane errors` are the two panels worth wiring first.

*Selector caveat: `ome_workload_cluster_*` and `ome_isvc_placement_candidate*` carry their own `cluster` label holding the member name, which shadows the collector's control-plane label, so those panels select on `cluster_id`. Renaming the metric label to `workload_cluster` would remove the special case.*
